summary: Leonard Bloomfield was a linguist who studied at Harvard, Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held posts at Cincinnati (~1909–1910), Illinois (~1910–1921), Ohio State (~1921–1927), Chicago (~1927–1940), and Yale (~1940–1949).

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology, studying under F. E. L. Priestley and doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held a post at the University of Toronto (attested 1991).

Leonard van der Kuijp, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earned his Ph.D. (~1976–1979) and D.Phil. (~1979–1983) at the University of Hamburg. He held positions at the University of Washington (attested 1989–1996) and Harvard University (1995).

Indologist Leopold von Schroeder studied at Dorpat/Tartu, Leipzig, Jena, and under Rudolf von Roth and Leo Meyer. He held posts at Tartu (~1882–1894), Innsbruck (~1894–1899), Vienna (~1899–1920), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1909–1920).

Leslie S. Kawamura was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther (~1970–1975) and served as a professor at the University of Calgary (~1976–2010).

Levi McLaughlin works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Princeton (PhD -2009) under Jacqueline I. Stone and at the University of Tokyo, later holding posts at Kokugakuin, Wofford, NUS, Iowa, and NC State (2012).

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under MA supervisor Ulrich Pagel. He has held posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018) and the University of Bonn (attested 2021).

Lewis Lancaster is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson (~1963–1968). He held a long career at the University of California, Berkeley (~1967–1998; Prof. ~1998).

Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist who served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center (2000).
Liang Cai works in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and held a post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas (attested 2014).
Lili Zheng is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Lilla Russell-Smith specializes in history/archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós, and earned her PhD at SOAS University of London.
Lin Heng is an Indologist who completed an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi (attested 2015).

Linda Jean LaMacchia specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under doctoral supervisor David M. Knipe (attested 2001).
Linda Learman is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentor Peter N. Gregory (attested 2005).
Linda Penkower is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University (-1993) and served as a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).
Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who studied under Bryan J. Cuevas (MA supervisor, attested 2007), Kathleen M. Erndl, and John Corrigan.
Ling Ji is a scholar of sinology who completed a PhD at the National University of Singapore under doctoral supervisor Yuet Keung Lo (attested 2014).

Indologist Lionel David Barnett studied at the University of Liverpool (~1888–1892) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1892–1896). He held posts at the British Museum (~1899–1936), University College London (~1906–1917), and SOAS University of London (~1917–1948).

Lionel Obadia works in religious and Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Lille University of Science and Technology (-1997). He held posts at INALCO (1996), KU Leuven (2000), EPHE (2002), Lille 3 (attested 2002), and Lyon 2 (attested 2010–2014).
